text:
emma: FYI customer VeloxHealth on Dedicated reported a morning spike where their routes started getting 429s and very high p95. They say autoscaler didn’t add capacity for ~3m. 

emma: Quick summary: pool=vip-velox-1, region=us-west-2, model=redwood-v2-opt, config shows min_replicas=1 max_replicas=12 cooldown_seconds=300 target_util=0.7. Metrics show CPU/GPUs pegged and queue depth rising. Customer sent request_ids: r-11f4, r-11f5, r-11f6.

raj: Can you paste the autoscaler event log and the HPA/scale status? Also which metric the autoscaler uses (cpu/qps/custom)?

emma: Paste below. This is what the autoscaler event stream shows around the incident (copied from our internal events):

```
2026-03-10T09:01:48Z autoscaler[event] pool=vip-velox-1 observed_util=0.68
2026-03-10T09:02:12Z autoscaler[event] pool=vip-velox-1 observed_util=0.82
2026-03-10T09:02:12Z autoscaler[decision] want_replicas=3 but cooldown_active until 2026-03-10T09:07:12Z
2026-03-10T09:03:05Z autoscaler[event] pool=vip-velox-1 queue_depth=24 latency_p95=1.8s
2026-03-10T09:04:30Z autoscaler[event] pool=vip-velox-1 observed_util=0.85
2026-03-10T09:05:20Z autoscaler[decision] cooldown expired, scale_up trigger -> scale to 3
```

emma: HPA-like status from control plane: desired=3 current=1 last_scale_time=2026-03-10T08:59:00 (note current stayed at 1 until our manual action)

lin: Wait, why did current stay at 1 after decision? Any errors from the node-provisioner or scheduler? Share the provisioner logs for that pool (the cluster indicated a 504 from infra-provisioner at 09:02:15).

emma: infra-provisioner logs snippet: 
```
2026-03-10T09:02:14Z provisioner ERROR allocation failed: insufficient_quota for instance-type a100-80gb
2026-03-10T09:02:15Z provisioner WARN retrying allocation after backoff
2026-03-10T09:03:30Z provisioner INFO allocation succeeded: node-id n-453
```

maria: So two things: (1) autoscaler triggered but provisioning hit a quota/backoff window -> slow node creation, (2) cold KV cache means new nodes take a while to warm up and serving latency stays high even after node spins up. Combined this gives the 3+ minute customer-visible lag.

raj: Agreed. Also the autoscaler decision was partly driven by CPU util but the immediate spike was queue depth / request rate. If the metric sampling window is long we get late detection. We should consider a request-rate based signal for this workload.

lin: For short-term mitigation I recommend: bump min_replicas to 3 for that pool and enable burst_capacity (we have reserved burst seats for enterprise customers). Also reduce the cooldown to 60s for aggressive scale-ups.

emma: I applied a temporary override at 09:06:30: min_replicas=3 cooldown_seconds=60, burst_capacity=enabled. Already seeing p95 drop from ~1.8s -> 280ms and queue depth fell to single digits. Customer confirmed 429s stopped at 09:08.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] pool=vip-velox-1 cooldown cleared, override=min_replicas=3 set by emma (support).

raj: Long-term fixes:
- add request_rate and queue_depth as autoscaler inputs (fast-reacting signals)
- reduce provisioning backoff when customer has reserved capacity / check quota ahead of high-traffic windows
- prewarm KV caches on new nodes via warmup hook (load small sample prompts) and track warmup completion metric
- add fallback routing to dedicated replica groups in another region when provisioning stalls

lin: Will file infra tickets: (1) quota check before scale, (2) faster provisioning path for reserved pools.

maria: I'll follow up with VeloxHealth CS and propose a dedicated reserved burst plan + recommended min_replicas for morning spikes.

emma: Repro steps for internal testing (do in staging):
1. Configure pool with min_replicas=1 cooldown=300 target_util=0.7
2. Generate synthetic burst (50 qps, model=redwood-v2-opt) for 2m from a single region
3. Watch autoscaler events; verify provisioning path and node-provisioner retries; observe time from trigger->node-ready->serving-ready

emma: Quick commands: 
- control plane: `rictl pools describe vip-velox-1 --events --last 1h`
- infra: `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/provisioner -l pool=vip-velox-1 --since=15m`

raj: I'll add a canary test that simulates quota exhaustion to validate our fallback flows.

lin: thx everyone. Action items: lin create infra tickets, raj add autoscaler metrics PR, maria handle CS follow-up, emma keep the override for 24h then evaluate. :thumbsup:
